::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** March 14th 1888  
**From:** Elderfield  
**Manuscript:** MS UCLA: collection 100: box 95
:::

My dear [Miss Butler](people/person_237.qmd)

I am afraid that there would not be good room for your paper till the end of the year—I mean Jany 1889. I agree with you that those old letters are full of deep interest, and such curiously unexpected traits come out in them. 

You will see in a note in the next [Monthly Packet](organizations/other_52.qmd) a very odd thing just disinterred out of some papers of my great-great-great grandfather about a tradition of Becket.[^1]

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: In a note signed by C.M.Y. appended to 'The Canterbury Relics' in *MP*  3s 15 (April 1888) 368, she quotes from the diary of James Yonge (1647-1721)  his seeing a dark line of corn in a field which was supposed to mark a path taken by Thomas à Becket.
